messages:
Maria P.: Ran a comparative perf run this morning: sliced-KV sharding + new batch-slice heuristic on three fabric setups (NVLink-local, PCIe-only single-node, EFA cross-node). Posting short findings and raw numbers.

Aj Patel: nice, high level first? :eyes:

Maria P.: TL;DR — NVLink best latency and throughput for TP+PP setups; PCIe-only shows higher kernel stalls due to bigger all-reduce cycles; EFA suffers for small microbatches but is ok once we increase slice width and enable async-reduce.

Leo Zhang: what model/config did you test?

Maria P.: 8B transformer, TP=2 PP=2, seq=2048 typical, kv-cache enabled. Two batching modes: baseline contiguous-batch and new slice-batch (the heuristic that slices large batches into sub-batches to improve comm/compute overlap).

Sophie L: can you paste the command + key perf logs?

Maria P.: command: ```
./run_infer --model redwood-8b --tp 2 --pp 2 --seq 2048 --batch 128 --slicing on --slice-width 32 --kv-shard sliced
```
perf snippet (averages over 5 runs):
```
NVLink-local: p99 latency=240ms, tokens/s=9800, allreduce-wait=18ms, kernel-occupancy=93%
PCIe-only: p99 latency=360ms, tokens/s=6100, allreduce-wait=48ms, kernel-occupancy=78%
EFA-cross: p99 latency=410ms, tokens/s=5400, allreduce-wait=65ms, kernel-occupancy=82%
```

Aj Patel: hmm allreduce-wait jumps a lot on EFA. Was that with the async-reduce patch?

Maria P.: initial run was without async-reduce. I retried with async-reduce=on and slice-width increased to 64:
```
EFA-cross (async-reduce on, slice=64): p99 latency=320ms, tokens/s=7200, allreduce-wait=22ms
```

Leo Zhang: so async-reduce + wider slices recovers most of the loss. Any regression with NVLink when increasing slice width?

Maria P.: NVLink flatlines after slice=32; slice=64 gives negligible improvements and slightly increases memory copy overhead. PCIe benefits moderately from slice-width=64 but still lags on allreduce due to host-mediated transfers.

Sophie L: interesting. Did you profile kernel selection changes? e.g., did the runtime pick fused-attn vs streaming for different fabrics?

Maria P.: yes — kernel selector favored fused-attn on NVLink. On EFA and PCIe we saw fallback to streaming-attn for long sequences because the cross-node latency made larger fused kernels hit timeout heuristics in the selector. I attached a short selector log:```
KERNEL_SELECTOR: seq=2048, candidate=fused_attn, est_latency=200ms, net_penalty=50ms -> pick=streaming_attn
```

bench-bot: perf-summary uploaded: https://bench.internal/runs/1967894321

Aj Patel: does the batch-slice heuristic cause more KV-cache churn? I worry about repeated KV transfers across nodes.

Maria P.: Good point. Slicing trades larger contiguous KV cache reuse for better comm/compute overlap. With sliced-KV sharding we keep per-slice KV local as much as possible; observed increased KV invalidations by ~6% on EFA when slice width small (16) because of more frequent cross-node fetches. Increasing slice width to 64 reduced invalidations below baseline.

Leo Zhang: any concrete change requests?

Maria P.: Suggested next steps: 1) make async-reduce default for cross-node fabric when slice-width >= 32; 2) update kernel-selector to incorporate fabric penalty heuristics (so fused_attn isn't penalized too aggressively on EFA if async-reduce enabled); 3) add a KV churn metric to console (token-level KV hit/miss + invalidation rate).

Sophie L: +1 for KV churn metric. Also we should add a small A/B where we pin fused kernel on EFA with async-reduce to measure worst-case.

Aj Patel: I'll pick up kernel-selector changes. tagging @Leo for async-reduce rollout plan.

Leo Zhang: noted. I'll test async-reduce rollout on staging with the bench harness.

infra-bot: deploy plan created: DPL-1173 async-reduce feature flag + monitoring -> staging by 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC

Maria P.: thanks all — saved raw traces to s3://redwood-perf/1967894321/ (selector logs, nvprof, ib-sockets). If anyone needs the binary diff I have a patch branch `slice-kv-efa-fix`.
